stem: A client without cancer receives a germline genetic-test result showing a pathogenic BRCA1 variant. Which explanation by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: The result means the client has an increased risk for several cancers, but it does not predict with certainty whether or when cancer will develop; individualized risk-management counseling and discussion with blood relatives are appropriate.
options.B: The result means the client already has occult breast or ovarian cancer even if current diagnostic evaluation is negative.
options.C: The result guarantees that the client will develop cancer, so routine screening is no longer useful.
options.D: The result has no implications for blood relatives because inherited BRCA variants affect only the person who was tested.

rationale: A is correct. NCI states that an inherited harmful/pathogenic BRCA1 or BRCA2 variant increases the risk of several cancers but cannot predict whether or when cancer will develop, and some carriers never develop cancer. NCI also supports individualized risk-management options such as enhanced screening and notes that results may be shared with blood relatives so they can better understand their own potential risk. B is incorrect because a germline pathogenic variant indicates susceptibility, not a current cancer diagnosis. C is incorrect because increased inherited risk is not a guarantee and screening/risk-reduction remain relevant. D is incorrect because inherited results can have implications for blood relatives, although no specific relative can be assumed to carry the variant without testing.
educational_objective: Interpret a germline pathogenic BRCA result as inherited cancer susceptibility rather than a cancer diagnosis or certainty, and recognize its implications for individualized prevention/screening and family risk communication.
source_organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health
source_document_title: BRCA Gene Changes: Cancer Risk and Genetic Testing Fact Sheet
source_locator: Sections 'What are BRCA1 and BRCA2?', 'Who should consider genetic counseling and testing for inherited harmful changes in BRCA1 and BRCA2?', 'What do BRCA1 and BRCA2 genetic test results mean?' — Positive result, and 'How can a person who has inherited a harmful change in BRCA1 or BRCA2 manage their risk of cancer?'.
source_claim_supported: Pathogenic germline BRCA variants increase cancer risk without guaranteeing cancer, may inform enhanced screening/risk reduction, and can have implications for blood relatives.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — prevention/early detection of health problems, health promotion and screening, and client education/risk reduction.
correction_summary: Reframed the source item with current NCI terminology for a germline pathogenic variant, removed deterministic genetic language, preserved family implications without assuming inheritance in any specific relative, and remapped the item to Health Promotion and Maintenance.
audit_findings: Fresh NCI review explicitly supports increased risk without certainty and family relevance of inherited test results.
The key avoids overclaiming that BRCA positivity proves current cancer or guarantees future cancer.
Distractors are realistic misconceptions and are each directly contradicted by NCI guidance.
Health Promotion and Maintenance is the stronger 2026 NCLEX mapping because the construct centers on inherited risk assessment, screening, prevention, and counseling.
Independent adversarial review found no second answer, cueing, deterministic inheritance claim, unsupported precision, or unresolved conflict.
